stance.text: I am asking for more automation of the quality checks, not for a full rebuild. The current plan does not go far enough for the reliability I need.
stance.correction: I did not mean that we should stop using the checks. I meant that we should automate them so the same quality is applied every time.

stance.text: I will not accept manual checks if they affect reliability. The proposal crosses my line.
stance.correction: I meant {reliability_ruth} proposed governed tools for quality checks, not manual checks. Please file this as a reliability constraint.

stance.text: You are counting my open source suggestion as a free concession on cost. Please acknowledge that I am accepting some manual work only to keep the project affordable.
stance.correction: I did not mean to trade governance for cheap tools. I meant we should use open source automation where possible and keep manual steps only when they save money.

stance.text: I, {efficiency_emilia}, did not agree to remove manual checks from the workflow. Please acknowledge that I asked for a cost and efficiency balance, not a hidden reduction of manual control.
stance.correction: I, {efficiency_emilia}, was talking about accepting some manual steps to keep costs low, not about accepting lower governance. Please file this as a cost and efficiency trade off, not as a change to the workflow level.

stance.text: I need governed data quality checks before we trust any model output. The current proposal leaves compliance gaps that I cannot accept.
stance.correction: I was not talking about optional dashboards or periodic reviews. I meant governed checks that enforce data quality and privacy rules in the production workflow.

stance.text: I will not approve automated quality checks if they increase costs. We will keep the checks manual.
stance.correction: You filed that as a preference, but it is a cost boundary. I meant I will not support automation unless the cost impact stays acceptable.

stance.text: I want more cost savings in the experiment tracking process, and this proposal does not do enough for that goal. I am not refusing, but I need stronger data operations savings.
stance.correction: I meant a cost savings request for experiment tracking, not a data quality issue. Please file this as a cost and data operations concern.

stance.text: You are taking my manual experiment tracking without naming it. Please acknowledge that I asked for that trade off.
stance.correction: That was a trade off, not a fixed requirement. I meant manual tracking only if it significantly reduces costs.

stance.text: This proposal takes away my cost control without saying so. Please acknowledge that trade off in the plan.
stance.correction: You filed this as a hard requirement, but it is a trade off. I would accept a less automated solution if it significantly reduces costs.

stance.text: This plan does not do enough to connect experiment tracking with our business goals. I need stronger alignment before we accept it.
stance.correction: When I said aligning experiment tracking with business goals, I meant it must improve operational capability and KPIs, not just add tracking.

stance.text: I want more than basic automated experiment tracking. It needs to make every run reproducible and easier to compare.
stance.correction: I am not saying the proposal is useless. I mean it should be treated as a reproducibility requirement, not a nice to have.

stance.text: I will not approve a workflow that leaves experiment tracking manual. We need automated tracking so every model run is reproducible.
stance.correction: I was not saying we need a new model registry. I meant experiment tracking must be automated end to end.

stance.text: I will not approve this proposal. It does not address the audit findings on model reproducibility.
stance.correction: This is a compliance requirement, not a preference. I meant that any solution must close the reproducibility gaps before we proceed.

stance.text: I think this proposal does not go far enough for our compliance needs. We need stronger experiment tracking controls, and I am not refusing the direction.
stance.correction: I meant a compliance requirement, not a general quality preference. Please file this as a security and governance need for experiment tracking.

stance.text: I will keep data labeling done by hand. I will not accept automation that reduces my control over the labeling process.
stance.correction: I did not object to all data operations. I only meant that hand labeling must stay under my control.

stance.text: I can work with manual labeling, but it is not enough for our data quality needs. We need stronger validation and clearer ownership of labeling rules.
stance.correction: I did not mean {data_dave} should skip automation entirely. I meant manual review should stay where judgment matters, with automated checks around it.

stance.text: The plan removes my labeling control without naming it. If we keep it partly manual, acknowledge that trade off.
stance.correction: You filed that as a hard refusal, but I only meant a partly manual labeling path. I would accept some automation if it clearly improves data quality.

stance.text: I am not refusing the plan, but it does not do enough for the efficiency goal I asked for. We need automated data validation before the next release.
stance.correction: I meant a specific request for automated data validation, not a general preference for every tool. Please record it as an efficiency requirement.

stance.text: I cannot approve this proposal. It does not enforce data governance, and I will not accept that.
stance.correction: I meant a hard requirement, not a preference. Any process without enforced data governance is unacceptable to me.

stance.text: I cannot approve this labeling plan. It must be fully governed before I accept it.
stance.correction: I was not talking about general data quality. I meant the labeling workflow itself must be fully governed.

stance.text: The proposal does not give me fully governed data labeling. I need stronger controls so the services I deploy stay reliable.
stance.correction: I am not saying the proposal is unacceptable. I am saying it must include governed labeling so model inputs stay reliable.

stance.text: The plan asks me to take on semi manual labeling work, but it does not name that cost. Please acknowledge that trade explicitly.
stance.correction: I am {reliability_ruth}, and I did not mean to propose a permanent semi manual labeling process. I meant we should test a semi manual step only if it improves data quality.

stance.text: The proposal gives the model registry too little governance. I want stronger controls and more oversight, not a lighter setup.
stance.correction: You filed this as a general data note, but I meant a governance requirement for the model registry. {data_dave} wants it governed, with more controls and clearer ownership.

stance.text: I, {data_dave}, need the proposal to acknowledge this. It takes the model registry decision from my team without saying so.
stance.correction: I did not mean we must source the model registry from a custom tool. I meant {data_dave} would accept another source if it meets our data quality and governance needs.

stance.text: As {efficiency_emilia}, I will not support a proposal that leaves the model registry ungoverned. That is a clear no from me.
stance.correction: I was not setting a KPI. I meant that I will not do my work without governance on the model registry.

stance.text: The proposal does not do enough for my goals. I need more than a basic automation.
stance.correction: You filed this under the wrong kind of intel. I meant it as a business objective, not just a technical task.

stance.text: I will not support a governed model registry. My team will not work with governance controls on registry changes.
stance.correction: I was not describing a missing registry. I was setting a limit on governance for the registry.

stance.text: I, {model_monica}, need the registry to handle versioning and promotion checks, not just a basic upload step. That proposal leaves too much manual work for me.
stance.correction: You logged this as a simple efficiency wish, but I meant a governed automation path for my model lifecycle. I was asking for stronger controls, not just fewer clicks.

stance.text: I need the proposal to acknowledge that I am giving up model registry automation for compliance. Please make that trade off explicit.
stance.correction: I did not mean that I reject automation. I meant that compliance must be ensured before the model registry is automated.

stance.text: I will not approve a model registry that is not governed. Governance is the minimum bar for production use.
stance.correction: You filed this as a preference, but I meant it as a hard requirement. The registry must be governed before I will support it.
